name: Corinthia Rome
positioning: Grand palazzo hotel on Piazza del Parlamento in Rome's historic Campo Marzio district, in a 1920s former Bank of Italy building
best_for: Travelers who want a central base among Rome's historic landmarks
Guests drawn to restored historic interiors and a Roman bathing-inspired spa

facts.text: Corinthia Rome occupies a grand palazzo on Piazza del Parlamento, in Rome's historic heart.
The hotel is in the historic Campo Marzio district.
The hotel is just moments from the Pantheon, the Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps.
The 1920s building served as the offices of the Bank of Italy until 1961.
Restoration of the building uncovered mosaics, stuccoes, cornices, painted ceilings and marble details.
The Corinthia Spa sits in the bank's former historic vault and is inspired by the ritual of Roman bathing.
The spa has a tepidarium, a calidarium and a frigidarium.
Rooms have high ceilings and large windows, with views of the city's rooftops or the quiet inner courtyard.
Rooms have marble bathrooms, and all rooms include books on art, culture and history.
From the Arte Suite, guests can see the Vatican.
Dining at the hotel is curated by chef Carlo Cracco, in his Roman debut.
Piazzetta, at the heart of the palazzo, is a lively open-kitchen and garden retreat.

highlights.text: In the spa, a path leads from two baths at different temperatures to a hammam, a sauna, an ice fountain and beds of heated black stones.
The Sala del Consiglio on the piano nobile has frescoes by Giulio Bargellini on the theme of prosperity.
The Theodoli Heritage Suite uses the Sala del Consiglio, where the bank's board of directors met, as its living room.
The Chigi Suite opens onto a large panoramic rooftop terrace.
The hotel faces Palazzo Montecitorio, the seat of the Italian parliament, near Via del Corso.

considerations.text: The building is listed, which presents some accessibility challenges in public areas; four guest rooms are designed for guests with mobility, hearing or visual impairments.
The spa is an underground retreat in the former bank vault, beneath the palazzo.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
